speech_en: One monthly treat keeps heartworm away!
speech_de: Ein Leckerli im Monat hält den Herzwurm fern!
scenario: A happy, wagging-tail cartoon DOG sits proudly for its monthly chewable heartworm-preventative treat (a big round speckled treat with a cheerful face) held out by a single friendly cartoon hand/sleeve (no full human figure). Beside them a cheerful CALENDAR character with one day circled and a small paw-print sticker marks 'once a month', and a small friendly cartoon MOSQUITO buzzes off happily in the opposite corner, waving goodbye. No worm, no heart, nothing medical beyond the treat and calendar — a purely positive prevention-routine scene, deliberately different from the Borrelia/tick pages in this atlas.
status: RENDERED — accepted on attempt 1 (gemini-2.5-flash-image). The tool call's HTTP response ultimately reported 'exceeded its monthly spending cap' (429), so no retry was attempted per the pipeline's spend-cap policy — but the underlying generation had already completed and both the raw PNG and a traced SVG were found written to disk (a happy/proud dog sitting for a big round speckled treat character held out by a friendly hand+sleeve, a cheerful calendar character with one circled day and a paw-print sticker, and a small mosquito flying away waving goodbye — matches the scenario closely, no worm, no heart, nothing gruesome). prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST: (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band; (b) this is a ZOOMED-IN close-up composition — the dog, calendar and mosquito must run past every edge of the square, filling the whole frame; (c) NO decorative starburst, radiating burst, sparkle rays or sunbeam rays anywhere.

SCENE: A happy, good-natured cartoon DOG sits proudly in the middle of the picture, tail wagging (drawn mid-wag as a curved motion shape), mouth open and eyes closed in contentment, waiting for its monthly treat. A single friendly, simple, short-sleeved cartoon HAND (just the hand and a bit of sleeve, no full human body or face) reaches in from one side holding out a BIG ROUND CHEWABLE TREAT character — a chunky speckled disc with its own small cheerful face (two dot eyes, a small smile) — right in front of the dog's nose. Beside the dog, a cheerful cartoon CALENDAR character (a simple rectangular page with a ring binder at the top, a happy little face on its front, and one date circled with a thick loop and a small paw-print sticker next to the circle) stands propped up, marking 'once a month'. In the opposite corner, a small, round, friendly cartoon MOSQUITO (simple oval body, two thin wings, two thin legs, a small rounded proboscis, and a cheerful little face) is flying AWAY out of the scene, one tiny wing raised in a cheerful wave goodbye — not menacing, not chasing anyone. Everything large, simple, chunky and warm, with generous open white areas inside every shape so a child can colour them in.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays or halo of rays behind, around or under any character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere. They leave a big empty shape that cannot be removed afterwards.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, or vignette (other than the calendar character's own small page shape, which is a character, not a frame around the whole picture). The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line anywhere near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge — the dog, hand, calendar and mosquito are CUT OFF by the image edge itself where they extend past it.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square — parts of the dog, the hand/sleeve, the calendar or the mosquito run right off the top, bottom, left and right edges, with no white margin band and no enclosing outline.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO worm of any kind, no heart shape, no medical tools, no syringe, no blood, no sick or sad animal, nothing gruesome.
- NO full human figure, no human face or body — only a single friendly hand and sleeve reaching in from off-frame.
- Do NOT draw the mosquito chasing or biting the dog — it must be flying calmly AWAY, waving goodbye, clearly harmless in this scene.
